summary:
The Tacna region stands under Peru's national framework; the national layer of criminal law, anti-discrimination protection, identity documents and facility access is carried by the Peru record.

On 19 April 2025 Marcia Paucara Cora, a 48-year-old trans woman, was found dead in a room of the Los 5 Titos hostel on Arias y Aragüez street in central Tacna. The autopsy recorded death by mechanical asphyxia through compression of the airways. She had entered the hostel on a Sunday with a man who registered under a false identity and left alone roughly two hours later carrying a white bag; hostel staff discovered the body when the rental period expired.

By 21 May 2025 police were analysing surveillance footage from inside and outside the hostel to trace the suspect's escape route, and no suspect had been identified. The victim had initially been processed as an unidentified person and was identified only through the hostel's cameras. Relatives denounced the killing and demanded police action.

Wayka reported on 27 May 2025 that the case is being investigated as a possible hate crime, meaning an offence motivated by prejudice and discrimination on grounds of the victim's sexual orientation or gender identity. The family and local LGTBIQ+ collectives held a vigil on Friday 23 May 2025 demanding justice, describing the killing as the reflection of a structural system of violence that silences trans lives.
tangentialFactors:
Two outlets covered the same homicide with different emphasis: the regional report Wayka carried the hate-crime investigation line, the autopsy finding and the vigil, while the national tabloid Trome concentrated on the police manhunt, the victim's initial unidentified status and the surveillance footage. Neither source supplies any comparative figure for Tacna against other Peruvian regions, and no ranking of Tacna by recorded incidents appears in the inventory.

Wayka's coverage attaches national context to the Tacna case, including Peru's absence of gender-identity-recognition legislation and of a hate-crime statute, a bathroom-access bill promoted by congressman Alejandro Muñante, and Public Prosecutor's Office counts of 84 criminal complaints concerning LGTB deaths between January 2012 and May 2021, of which 55.8% of victims were gay men and 36.4% trans women. Those figures are national and belong to the Peru record rather than to this region's assessment.
localsOnly:
Local LGTBIQ+ collectives in Tacna organised the 23 May 2025 vigil alongside the victim's family and continue to press for the killing to be treated as motivated by prejudice against trans people, framing it as part of a structural pattern in which trans lives are silenced.

The investigation sits with Tacna's police and prosecution service. As of the 21 May 2025 report no suspect had been identified and the evidentiary base was the hostel's camera system and the surrounding street footage; the family has publicly called for police action rather than a closed file.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the killing of Marcia Paucara Cora will ultimately be charged or convicted as a hate crime is unresolved in the sources, which stop in late May 2025; the inventory records only that it is under investigation as a possible hate crime and that no suspect had been identified at that point.

No Tacna-specific provisions on public facilities, identity documents, healthcare access or anti-discrimination redress appear in the inventory. Whether the region applies or diverges from national rules in these areas is not sourced here and is not asserted.

The cause of death comes from Wayka's account of the autopsy; Trome's earlier report does not carry a medical finding, so the two accounts are consistent but not equivalent in evidentiary detail.
